subject: AI & Agents
title: ResNet: Going Deeper Than Ever
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on ResNet: Going Deeper Than Ever.

hook.text: A 152-layer network should be impossible to train. Residual connections made it not just possible but dominant.

buildup.text: Deeper networks suffered from vanishing gradients — learning signals faded to zero.

discovery.text: ResNet added skip connections that let gradients flow through shortcut paths around layers.

twist.text: The insight was simple: let each layer learn the difference from identity, not the full transformation.

climax.text: ResNet won ImageNet 2015 and its skip connections now appear in virtually every deep network.

punchline.text: The secret to going deeper: let information take shortcuts.

quiz.question: What problem did ResNet's skip connections solve?
options: Vanishing gradients that prevented training very deep networks

details.summary: ResNet introduced skip connections in 2015, solving the degradation problem that prevented training very deep neural networks. It enabled networks with 152 layers and won the ImageNet competition decisively.
details.whyItMatters: ResNet made deep learning truly deep. Skip connections became a standard building block used across virtually all modern neural network architectures, from vision to language models.
takeaways: ResNet solved the degradation problem in very deep networks
Skip connections let gradients flow through hundreds of layers
The technique became standard across all of modern deep learning

faq.question: What is the degradation problem ResNet solved?
faq.answer: Adding more layers to neural networks should improve performance, but in practice accuracy degraded. ResNet's skip connections let layers learn residual changes, making it possible to train networks 10x deeper.

faq.question: Why are skip connections so important?
faq.answer: They allow gradients to flow directly through the network during training, preventing the vanishing gradient problem. This simple idea enabled the deep architectures that power modern AI systems.
